# kamishibai

> kamishibai turns a list of words into an illustrated Anki deck — one card per word with a native example sentence, native-speaker audio, and a manga-style panel — using Google Gemini. It runs as an interactive terminal UI or as an asynchronous, session-based console flow built for agents.

This file documents the **console (session) flow**. Running `kamishibai` with no arguments opens the interactive TUI instead, which is out of scope here.

A session is a persistent, curatable unit of work an agent drives across separate invocations. It moves through stages:

1. **understood** — `new` understands each `--word` (or imports a cards JSON) and creates the session. The session now holds curatable candidates: per word, the senses the model proposed.
2. **(curate)** — optional: `select` which senses become cards, `exclude` a word, or `correct` a word to add senses. Each keeps the session understood.
3. **generating** — `generate` commits the curated plan and starts a managed background worker that produces the artifacts and publishes.
4. **published** — every committed card made the deck. `result` returns the finished cards; `regenerate` re-rolls committed cards.

A run where some cards exhaust their retries ends **partial** — the deck holds the rest, and `regenerate --failed` then `generate` fills the gaps. A run where no card survives ends **failed**.

Commands may run concurrently: edits serialize and all apply, and only one worker can generate a session at a time (a second `generate`, or any edit while one runs, is refused until it finishes or is cancelled).

Generation is slow (Gemini per artifact, and the first publish parses system fonts for the PDF — expect tens of seconds). Poll `status` at a relaxed interval; do not tight-loop. Re-running is idempotent and cache-backed, so a killed `generate` resumes and only fills in what is missing. The interactive TUI (`kamishibai` with no arguments, or `kamishibai open [<id>]`) shares this same session model, so `ls`/`status` see interactive runs too.

## Output contract

Output defaults to **plain text**; pass `--json` (placed after the verb) to get exactly one JSON document on stdout instead. Plain mode still needs no `jq`/`grep`/`sed`; the rules below describe it:

- **stdout carries the one capturable value**, bare: `new`/`select`/`exclude`/`correct`/`generate`/`regenerate` print the session id (but `generate --wait` prints the three deck/pdf/dir paths instead, like `result`); `result --deck|--pdf|--dir` print one path. So `id=$(kamishibai new --word bank)` captures exactly the id.
- **stderr carries everything else**: the understood-senses preview, progress, hints, errors. Every error is one `kamishibai: …` line (in both modes).
- `status`/`result`/`ls` print line-oriented text to stdout; `-q`/`--quiet` reduces any command to its bare capturable value and silences the stderr narration (`status -q` → the phase word, `result -q` → the three paths, `ls -q` → ids, mutating verbs → the id).
- Exit codes are the script signal: `0` ok · `2` usage · `3` no such session · `4` not ready yet · `5` ambiguous (an omitted id matched several sessions) · `1` other error. **For any invocation accepted in both modes they are identical — `--json` changes representation, never the signal** (its own grammar conflicts — `-q`, the `result` selectors, `open` — are refused with exit `2` before the session is even looked up), and it does not change locking, idempotency, or session semantics either.

### Omitting the session id

Every verb's `<id>` is optional. When omitted, the command resolves the session once, at invocation: if exactly one session exists it is used (even a finished one); otherwise, if exactly one session is **unfinished** (`understood`/`generating`/`interrupted` — anything except `published`/`partial`/`failed`/`cancelled`) it is used; otherwise nothing runs and the command prints the newest five sessions as `ls` lines on stdout (newest first, plus `…and N more — kamishibai ls` when more exist) and exits `5`. With no sessions at all it exits `3`. When resolution picks a session, plain mode says so once on stderr: `using session <id>`. Note the cascade prefers the session you are working on, not the one that is done: with a published deck and a fresh understood session, `result` resolves to the fresh one and exits `4` — pass the id to read an older session's result.

### JSON mode

`--json` prints exactly one document per invocation on stdout — the success document, or on any failure the error envelope `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"usage|not_found|not_ready|ambiguous|operational","exit":2|3|4|5|1,"message":"…"}}` (the `kamishibai: …` stderr line still appears). The `ambiguous` envelope additionally carries a top-level `sessions` array — the newest five candidates, newest first, with the same item shape as `ls --json`. `--json` is mutually exclusive with `-q` and with the `result` selectors `--deck`/`--pdf`/`--dir` (exit `2`); `open` is interactive and refuses it. clap parse errors (unknown flag, `--json` placed before the verb) stay plain text outside the envelope. The schema evolves additively only: keys are never renamed or removed.

Every stateful verb (`new`, `select`, `exclude`, `correct`, `generate`, `regenerate`, `cancel`, `status`) returns the same **session document** — mutating verbs return the post-mutation state, so no follow-up `status` is needed:

```json
{"ok":true,"session":"fr-20260612_091500_ab3x","created":"2026-06-12T09:15:00Z",
 "pair":{"from":"en","to":"fr"},"senses":"primary","source":"words",
 "out":"/abs/out","phase":"generating","words":["canard"],
 "worker":{"pid":4242,"alive":true},
 "progress":{"term":"canard","artifact":"scene"},
 "candidates":{"count":1,"selected":1,"items":[
   {"term":"canard","included":true,"senses":[
     {"number":1,"tag":"zool.","understanding":"a duck","selected":true},
     {"number":2,"understanding":"a hoax","selected":false}]}]},
 "cards":{"total":1,"ready":0,"failed":0,"items":[
   {"term":"canard","understanding":"a duck","state":"building",
    "artifacts":{"meta":true,"sound":true,"scene":false,"picture":false}}]},
 "result":{"deck":"/o/fr.apkg","pdf":"/o/fr.pdf","dir":"/o","cards":1,"failed":0},
 "error":"…"}
```

Presence rules: `phase` is the live reconciliation (`status -q`'s 7-word vocabulary — the terminal-phase warning below applies identically); `candidates` appears while the record holds curatable candidates, `cards` once a plan is committed, and `worker`/`progress`/`result`/`error` only when present — absent fields are omitted, never `null`. `senses[].number` is 1-based and matches `select --sense`; `cards[].state` is `ready|failed|building|pending`.

Other shapes: `result --json` → `{"ok":true,"session":…,"pair":…,"phase":…,"paths":{"deck":…,"pdf":…,"dir":…},"cards":N,"failed":M,"items":[…]}` where `items` are strict cards-JSON entries — the exact `new --build` schema, so they round-trip into a new session. `ls --json` → `{"ok":true,"sessions":[{"id":…,"pair":…,"created":…,"phase":…,"cards":{"total":N,"ready":M}}]}` (`selected: N` instead of `cards` before a plan is committed; the array may be empty). `rm --json` → `{"ok":true,"removed":"<id>"}`. `cache-path --json` → `{"ok":true,"cache":"/…"}`.

`generate --wait --json` streams NDJSON **events on stderr** and prints the one final session document on stdout (`published` or `partial`; a run where every card failed exits `1` with the error envelope instead — `status <id> --json` then shows `"phase":"failed"`; a cancel that raced in yields `ok:true` with `"phase":"cancelled"` and no `result`, so gate on `phase`, not `ok`). Events: `{"event":"generating","cards":N}`, `{"event":"step","term":…,"artifact":"meta|sound|scene|picture","status":"ok|cache|retry|fail","attempt":1,"ceiling":3}` (attempt/ceiling only on retry), `{"event":"publishing"}`, `{"event":"warning","message":…}`. stderr lines that do not parse as JSON are lower-layer narration (model downloads etc.) — ignore them; strictness is guaranteed only for stdout.

## Requirements

- A Gemini API key is required for any flow that calls Gemini: set `GEMINI_API_KEY` (it wins) or reuse a key saved through the interactive Welcome screen. `GEMINI_API_KEY` need not be set when a saved key exists.
- The first OCR-backed run downloads PP-OCRv5 model files into the cache.

## Commands

- `kamishibai new (--word WORD [--word WORD …] | --words FILE | --build FILE) [--to LANG] [--from LANG] [--senses primary|all] [--out DIR] [--id NAME] [--generate] [-q | --json]` — understand the words and create a session in the **understood** stage. Exactly one input form is required: repeated `--word` flags (one card per word), `--words FILE` (one word per line, `-` for stdin), or `--build FILE` (a strict cards JSON path or `-`, skips understanding; its entries carry the language pair, so `--from`/`--to`/`--senses` are rejected with it). `--senses` sets the initial sense selection (`primary` = the top sense; `all` = every sense); `select` overrides it later. `--generate` commits and starts the worker at once. Prints the understood senses to stderr and the bare session id to stdout.
- `kamishibai select [<id>] --card TERM --sense 1,3 [--json]` — choose which 1-based senses of a card become cards (and re-include it). Resets the session to understood.
- `kamishibai exclude [<id>] --card TERM [--json]` — drop a card from the plan while keeping it visible in the understanding. Resets to understood.
- `kamishibai correct [<id>] --card TERM --note "..." [--json]` — ask Gemini to add senses to a card from an instruction. Resets to understood.
- `kamishibai generate [<id>] [--wait] [-q | --json]` — commit the curated plan (deriving it from the selected senses) and start a managed background worker that generates the missing artifacts then publishes; prints the id and returns at once. `--wait` runs it in the foreground, streaming progress. Fails if nothing is selected.
- `kamishibai status [<id>] [-q | --json]` — before a plan is committed: the curatable candidates with their senses and selection; after: per-card artifact progress. Read from the cache (no Gemini). `-q` prints only the phase word (`understood`/`generating`/`published`/`partial`/`failed`/`interrupted`/`cancelled`).
- `kamishibai open [<id>]` — open the session in the interactive TUI, resuming from the cache.
- `kamishibai result [<id>] [--deck | --pdf | --dir | -q | --json]` — the finished cards (term, meaning, both example sentences, pronunciation, hint) plus the deck/pdf/dir paths. The selectors (`--deck`/`--pdf`/`--dir`) are mutually exclusive, cannot combine with `-q`, and print exactly one path; bare `-q` prints the three paths. Works once the session is **published** or **partial** (a partial run prints `cards N in deck · M failed`); exits `4` otherwise.
- `kamishibai regenerate [<id>] (--failed | --card TERM [--note "..."]) [--json]` — drop cached artifacts so the next `generate` rebuilds them: every unfinished card with `--failed`, or one card by `--card`. With `--note`, Gemini first rewrites that card from the instruction (a Gemini call), then its artifacts are dropped; a later curation discards the rewrite. Prints the id.
- `kamishibai cancel [<id>] [--json]` — stop the running worker (leaves an already-finished session — published/partial/failed — unchanged). Always exits `0` with a correct final phase, even when it races the worker finishing.
- `kamishibai ls [-q | --json]` — list sessions (id · pair · phase · progress; `-- / N` before a plan is committed, `ready/total` after); `-q` prints only ids.
- `kamishibai rm [<id>] [--cache] [--json]` — delete the session, and with `--cache` its cached card folders.
- `kamishibai cache-path [--json]` — print the cache directory.

Supported language codes: `en`, `zh`, `es`, `ja`, `fr`, `de`, `ru`, `it`, `pt`, `el`.

## Example renderings

`kamishibai new --word "you're gonna get yours" --word bank --from ru --to en` (preview on **stderr**, id on **stdout**):

```
understanding 2 word(s) · ru → en
you're gonna get yours
  card  разг.   Идиом. «ты получишь по заслугам», обещание неизбежного наказания за проступки.
bank
  card  фин.    Сущ. «банк», организация для хранения денег.
  skip          Сущ. «берег» реки, озера, любого природного водоёма.
session en-…_0cfy · senses=primary · generate: kamishibai generate en-…_0cfy
```
```
en-…_0cfy
```

`kamishibai status <id>` while **understood** (stdout) — the curatable candidates, `*` marks a selected sense:

```
session  en-…_0cfy
pair     ru → en
senses   primary
phase    understood
words    2 understood · 2 card(s) selected
word  you're gonna get yours   card
  *  1  разг.   Идиом. «ты получишь по заслугам», обещание неизбежного наказания за проступки.
word  bank   card
  *  1  фин.    Сущ. «банк», организация для хранения денег.
     2          Сущ. «берег» реки, озера, любого природного водоёма.
out   /Users/you/kamishibai-out
```

Curate, then commit — e.g. keep only the river-bank sense of `bank`, then start generating:

```
kamishibai select en-…_0cfy --card bank --sense 2   # stderr: selected sense(s) 2 of 'bank'
kamishibai generate en-…_0cfy
```

`kamishibai status <id>` while **generating** (stdout) — `meta:ok scene:--` means present/absent; `status -q` prints just `generating`:

```
session  en-…_0cfy
pair     ru → en
senses   primary
phase    generating
worker   pid 48213 alive
cards    2 total · 1 ready · 0 failed
card  you're gonna get yours   meta:ok sound:ok scene:ok picture:ok   ready
card  bank                     meta:ok sound:ok scene:-- picture:--   building
out   /Users/you/kamishibai-out
```

`kamishibai result <id>` (stdout) — the finished cards plus paths:

```
session  en-…_0cfy
pair     ru → en
deck     /Users/you/kamishibai-out/en_….apkg
pdf      /Users/you/kamishibai-out/en_….pdf
dir      /Users/you/kamishibai-out

card 1/2  you're gonna get yours   importance 4
  meaning  ты получишь по заслугам, тебе это ещё аукнется
  say      jʊr ˈɡʌnə ˈɡɛt jʊrz
  en       Keep acting like a bully, and you're gonna get yours sooner or later.
  ru       Продолжай вести себя как задира, и «ты получишь по заслугам» рано или поздно.
  hint     Не официальный судебный вердикт punish, а зловещее обещание уличной мести.
```

`generate --wait` streams progress on stderr with stable tokens, then prints the three paths on stdout:

```
generating 2 card(s)…
  cache  you're gonna get yours · meta
  ok     bank · meta
  retry  bank · picture (1/3)
  ok     bank · picture
building deck and report…
done: 2 card(s) published
```

## Capturing values (no filtering)

```
id=$(kamishibai new --word "you're gonna get yours" --word bank --from ru --to en)
kamishibai exclude "$id" --card bank          # optional curation, prints "$id" again
kamishibai generate "$id"
while :; do
  case "$(kamishibai status "$id" -q)" in
    published) break ;;
    partial) echo "some cards failed; the deck is partial" >&2; break ;;
    failed|interrupted|cancelled) echo "generation did not finish" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *) sleep 5 ;;
  esac
done
deck=$(kamishibai result "$id" --deck)
```

`status -q` can return any of `understood`/`generating`/`published`/`partial`/`failed`/`interrupted`/`cancelled`, so a poll loop must break on every terminal phase (`published`, `partial`, `failed`, `interrupted`, `cancelled`), not just `published`, or it spins forever on a failed run. `partial` means the deck was published but some cards failed.

When `jq` is available, `kamishibai status "$id" --json | jq -r .phase` is the structural alternative, and `status --json` carries everything (phase, per-card artifacts, paths) in one call.

## Cache

The cache directory is printed by `kamishibai cache-path` (macOS `~/Library/Caches/kamishibai`; Linux `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/kamishibai` or `~/.cache/kamishibai`; override with `KAMISHIBAI_CACHE`).

```
<cache>/cards/<from>-<to>/<key>/      meta.json  scene.json  voice.wav  illustration.jpg
<cache>/understanding/<from>-<to>/<key>.json
<cache>/sessions/<id>/                session.json  worker.log
<cache>/ocr-models/                   shared OCR model files
```

`<key>` is a short content hash. `status` derives each card's readiness by checking which artifact files exist; deleting a card's folder forces it to regenerate on the next `generate`. `session.json` additionally holds the typed words, the curated candidates, and the committed plan.

## Input

For `new` each word is one `--word` flag (one card per word); `--words FILE` reads one word per line and `--words -` reads stdin.

For `new --build FILE` the input is a strict cards JSON path (or `-` for stdin). Every field is required and unknown fields are rejected:

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "term": "lantern",
      "meaning": "a portable lamp",
      "pronunciation": "LAN-tern",
      "transcription": "/lantern/",
      "importance": 7,
      "source": {
        "sentence": "I carried a lantern through the dark hallway.",
        "lang": "en",
        "highlight": "lantern",
        "hint": "portable light",
        "context": "a simple everyday sentence"
      },
      "target": { "sentence": "Ich trug eine Laterne durch den dunklen Flur.", "lang": "de" }
    }
  ]
}
```

`importance` is an integer 1–10; text fields and language codes must be non-empty.
